problem: 640 is not the number of worst-case rule checks. For n = 4 and |P| = 10 the number of (split, rule) checks is |P| × Σ over ℓ=2..n of (n−ℓ+1)(ℓ−1) = 10 × (3·1 + 2·2 + 1·3) = 10 × 10 = 100. The value 640 is just n³·|P| = 64 × 10, a loose upper bound, and writing 'O(n³|P|) = 640' misuses O as an equality. A student copying this answer gives a wrong count.
fix: Cells = n(n+1)/2 = 10. Split points = 10, rules = 10, so 100 rule checks; the asymptotic bound is O(n³·|P|), which for n = 4 and |P| = 10 is at most 640.

problem: The definition 'every rule is A → BC or A → a' leaves out the standard exception S → ε (the start variable may derive the empty string). Because of this, the chapter never says what CYK does with w = ε, yet it claims CYK answers whether any string w is in L(G). As written, CYK would reject ε even when ε ∈ L(G).
fix: Every rule is A → BC with B, C variables, or A → a with a a terminal; CNF also allows the extra rule S → ε (S the start variable). CYK as described handles only |w| ≥ 1, so check w = ε separately: it is in L(G) exactly when S → ε is a rule.

problem: The lead says membership costs 'about n³ rule checks', but Section 2 correctly gives O(n³·|P|) with |P| the number of rules. The two statements disagree, and the lead's version is only right for a fixed grammar.
fix: Membership costs about n³·|P| rule checks for |w| = n and |P| rules; for a fixed grammar this is O(n³).

problem: Earley and GLR are not asymptotically faster than CYK: both also run in O(n³) time in the worst case (O(n²) or O(n) for restricted/unambiguous grammars). Calling them simply 'faster' can mislead a student into thinking CYK is outclassed in the worst case.
fix: Faster in practice, not in the worst case: Earley and GLR also take O(n³) on general grammars, but they avoid the CNF conversion and run in O(n²) or O(n) for many real grammars, which is why compilers use them.

problem: The cell V[1,1] (row 'len 1', cell 0, holding A) is marked 'live', but nothing in the text explains what 'live' means. A reader cannot tell whether it signals the base case or a rule being used.
fix: Remove the 'live' mark, or state in the caption that it marks a length-1 base cell filled from A → a.
